title: Why Software Gets Harder to Change Over Time
summary:
Why do applications that start simple become so difficult to change?

Enrique Medina Montenegro, author of Clean Applications with Hexagonal Architecture, explains how tightly coupled business logic, frameworks, databases, and external services can make every change harder than the last—and why clear boundaries matter.

title: BREAKTHROUGH: A Bengaluru Startup Just Switched on India's First Private Nuclear Fusion Reactor
summary:
India's first private nuclear fusion reactor, Pragya, is now online in Bengaluru. We analyze what this compact tokamak means for energy.

A Bengaluru startup has activated Pragya, a compact tokamak designed to advance plasma control and engineering standards. While not yet generating commercial power, the facility serves as a vital testbed for fusion engineering, marking a significant milestone for India's role in global clean energy technology research.

The global timeline for fusion power remains ambitious, with projects like ITER targeting 2039 for operation. This report examines how private infrastructure is accelerating the development of the India tech ecosystem by focusing on the fundamental physics required to sustain fusion reactions.

title: EXPOSED: NITI Aayog Wants a Second Bengaluru but Karnataka Already Tried This and It Did Not Work
summary:
Niti Aayog is pushing for a second Bengaluru to manage growth, but can Karnataka replicate the city's success?

Niti Aayog has advised the Karnataka government that Bengaluru cannot sustain the state's rapid growth indefinitely. The Vice Chairman of Niti Aayog recently suggested to CM DK Shiv Kumar that the state should proactively establish a second Bengaluru to manage future development, presenting a map of potential twin city regions.

While the proposal aims to alleviate pressure on the capital, historical attempts at similar urban planning initiatives in the state have faced significant execution hurdles. We analyze the feasibility of these twin city regions and why previous efforts to decentralize infrastructure growth have struggled to gain traction, highlighting the complexities inherent in Karnataka development.

title: Stop Being Busy Being Busy
summary: In episode 1023 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Aishwarya Srinivasan, Co-Founder of The Gen Academy about her productivity framework, emphasizing saying 'no' to more things, having laser-focused intention, and regularly zooming out to re-evaluate priorities. She explains that it's easy to get caught in the trap of 'busy being busy' and that periodically stepping back to assess why you're doing certain tasks is crucial for aligning efforts with bigger goals. This approach helps maintain consistency and focus on what truly matters.

title: Agentic AI: The Shift from Automation to Autonomous Action
summary:
Agentic is in almost every AI conversation right now. Here is what it actually means, and how an agent differs from an assistant that only answers questions.

An AI agent takes a goal and works out the steps itself. Instead of someone manually pulling reports, running analysis and flagging accounts, the agent accesses the data, identifies at-risk customers, prioritizes them and surfaces the list ready to act on.

Terms covered:
- AI Agent: an AI that acts on a goal rather than responding to a prompt
- Agentic AI: systems that operate across multiple steps, decide along the way and adapt when something goes wrong
- Agentic: what the word signals when it describes a workflow, a platform or a process

Real examples: churn reduction in retail, patient follow-ups in healthcare, overnight compliance checks in financial services, live rerouting in logistics.

title: ATLAS Model - The Future of 3D AI Space
summary:
World Labs Atlas is a new omni world model for spatial intelligence from Fei-Fei Li’s company. It generates, reconstructs, and simulates 3D worlds from text, images, video, and camera poses, not just flat clips.

Atlas claims pixel-perfect camera control, up to 1 minute of 1440p video, sparse-view 3D reconstruction, explicit 3D output as point clouds and 3D Gaussian splats, video reframing / bullet-time effects, and real-to-sim workflows for robotics. It is described as a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer with a shared spatial context.

This video asks whether Atlas is a breakthrough or an upgrade on methods that already exist: text-to-video models like Sora and other camera-controlled generators, novel view synthesis, NeRF, 3D Gaussian splatting, photogrammetry and multi-view stereo, COLMAP-style reconstruction, and specialist sparse-view models such as VGGT, Depth Anything, Pi3, and MapAnything. We also compare it to World Labs’ earlier Marble product and to the broader world-model race (spatial intelligence, embodied AI, robot simulation).

Topics covered: Atlas explained, world models vs LLMs, camera-controlled video generation, 3D reconstruction from one photo or a few photos, Gaussian splats, real-to-sim-to-real, VFX from phone cameras, and whether one omni model can beat specialized 3D pipelines.

title: EXPOSED: India Is Training Millions for AI Jobs That Nobody at Entry Level Can Actually Get
summary:
While India is training millions of students in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and agentic workflows, employers simultaneously report an acute shortage of specialized AI talent. As enterprise teams become leaner and IT services majorly shift away from traditional mass campus recruitment, entry-level pathways are undergoing a fundamental transformation. With global capability centers (GCCs) hiring selectively for specialized, high-value skill sets, early-career candidates face a paradox: how do junior professionals gain experience if AI automation absorbs entry-level tasks?

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with three human resource and talent acquisition leaders: Deependra Mathur (CHRO, WebSol), Maya Nair (Executive Director, Grafton Recruitment India), and Saravanan Balasundaram (Founder & CEO, Han Digital Solution). They analyze macro employment numbers, the K-shaped AI job market, pre-qualified fresher hiring in GCCs, Tier-2 expansion, and why domain expertise remains essential alongside technical AI skills.

Can India's tech ecosystem bridge the gap between AI upskilling and sustainable entry-level employment?

title: EXPOSED: The Founder Whose Valuation Was Cut 80 Percent Says His Investors Got It Completely Wrong
summary:
From Elance to Gupshup AI Agents: Can AI Agents Replace Traditional Apps?

In the late 1990s, when the internet was still taking shape, Beerud Sheth co-founded Elance (now Upwork, a publicly traded company generating nearly $800 million annually), pioneering the global gig economy. He later co-founded Gupshup, a conversational messaging platform that today serves over 50,000 businesses across 100+ countries. Today, Gupshup is building autonomous AI agents that move beyond passive query answering to execute complex, multi-step enterprise workflows across messaging and voice channels.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Beerud Sheth, Co-Founder & CEO of Gupshup, to explore thirty years of technology cycles, from the early web and mobile shifts to generative and agentic AI. They discuss the death of traditional per-seat SaaS models, embedding context and guardrails into enterprise AI, how voice AI agents operate at one-tenth the cost of human call centers, and why conversational interfaces are replacing traditional websites, search engines, and mobile apps.

Will autonomous AI agents become the primary interface between businesses and consumers?

title: WeatherNext 3: More accurate, timely, and local weather forecasts
summary:
WeatherNext 3: More accurate, timely, and local weather forecasts 

Predicting the weather is one of the oldest, most complex challenges we face. Traditional numerical weather prediction models are powerful, but they can be slow to run and costly at a global scale. WeatherNext 3 takes a different approach. Built on a fundamentally different architecture, WeatherNext 3 learns directly from real-world observations, including live satellite feeds and ground-level weather station data.


What makes WeatherNext 3 different?
Hourly refresh: While traditional models typically refresh every six hours, WN3 produces a fresh forecast every single hour.
Hyper-Local resolution: Native 5km resolution for temperature and humidity, enabling better detail for coastal regions, mountains, and urban areas.
Actionable data: Includes variables like 100m wind speeds for wind energy management and detailed cloud/radiation metrics for solar energy planning.
Global reach: Delivering high-resolution insights everywhere.
You can now use WeatherNext 3 through Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps and more. 

Learn more: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/
Read the full paper: https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/papers/weathernext_3.pdf
Disclaimer: For official weather forecasts, severe weather warnings, and public safety advisories, please refer to your local meteorological agency or national weather service.

title: ALERT: India's Private Space Race Has One Fatal Flaw and It Has Nothing to Do With Rockets
summary:
India's private space exploration sector faces a critical financial hurdle regarding new insurance requirements for operators.

IN-SPACe has proposed a 500,000 rupee third-party coverage mandate for private companies, but experts are questioning if this amount is sufficient to manage the immense liability risks inherent in modern orbital missions. Under the 1972 Liability Convention, India remains internationally responsible for damages caused by objects launched from its territory, creating a complex legal landscape for startups.

This video breaks down why current space insurance costs can reach 30 percent of a mission's total value, effectively burdening new firms. We explore the underdeveloped nature of this market, where only a small fraction of satellites in low Earth orbit are actually covered. The analysis explains why a standard rocket launch involves risks that far exceed current proposed coverage limits and discusses potential solutions like catastrophic risk pools.

title: Is This Chip Smarter Than a GPU?
summary:
GPUs use billions of tiny 1-volt transistors to run code. Power electronics use just one highly engineered device to control grid power.

Drew Baglino (Founder & CEO of Heron Power, ex-Tesla SVP) explains how a single silicon carbide device, smaller than a GPU, can block 10,000 volts.

Old switches used a physical arm swinging through the air to stop high-voltage electricity. Power electronics do the same thing inside a solid material.

title: EXCLUSIVE: The Jet Engine Engineer Who Built a $500 Million AI Company in Under Two Years
summary:
Articul8 AI Hits $500M Valuation: Startup Secures $90M Contract Value

In mission-critical industries like aerospace, automotive, and financial services, an AI error is not just a software bug report: it is a multi-million-dollar liability. Spun out of Intel and AWS leadership by former GE Aerospace engineer Arun K. Subramaniyan, Articul8 AI has crossed $90 million in Total Contract Value (TCV) across 29 paying enterprise customers and achieved a $500 million valuation. Rather than relying solely on general-purpose frontier LLMs, Articul8’s platform deploys a domain-specific "correctness stack" that integrates deterministic business rules and independent verifiers directly into generative models.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Arun K. Subramaniyan, Founder & CEO of Articul8 AI, to decode enterprise AI deployment at scale. They discuss transitioning from aerospace fault resilience to software reliability, solving the final 10% accuracy gap that stalls enterprise pilots, federated data perception without data migration, the unit economics of training and inference compute, and why domain-specific language models are replacing generic LLMs in global corporations.

Can domain-specific correctness stacks solve the hallucination gap and drive production-grade enterprise AI?

title: BREAKING: Assam Is Building Its Own Satellite and 13 Indian Space Companies Want to Make It
summary:
Assam is launching its own Earth observation satellite system, marking a major shift in India news and regional governance.

The Assam State Space Application Center has officially shortlisted 13 companies, including Tata Advanced Systems and Pixxel, to build the Assam SAT system. This project moves the state from buying satellite data to owning its own space-based assets. By adopting a Design, Build, Launch, Operate, Train, and Transfer model, the state aims to gain internal expertise to manage floods, infrastructure, and land monitoring effectively.

This initiative highlights the rapid growth of the private space sector in the country, which has seen significant funding recently. As Assam takes this step, it could provide a replicable model for other regions looking to advance their own space exploration capabilities through targeted public-private partnerships.

title: Strange Geometric Shapes Found Inside AIs — Tom McGrath
summary:
Tom McGrath is co-founder and Chief Scientist at Goodfire, and a former Google DeepMind researcher. He joins Tim Scarfe to ask what neural networks actually learn, whether their internal representations converge on structures in the world, and whether interpretability can extract new scientific knowledge rather than merely explain model outputs.

Beginning with AlphaZero and learned modularity, the conversation moves into neural geometry: concept manifolds, reusable computation inside Llama, and why activation steering can fail when it pushes a model off-manifold. McGrath then makes the case for intentional design, using interpretability as part of the training loop. They examine controlled generalisation, features as rewards, predictive data debugging, and the uncomfortable fact that a model may recognise a hallucination or reward hack and still produce it.

The discussion closes on grader awareness, oversight and collusion between adaptive agents, then returns to sparse autoencoders. SAEs are useful, McGrath argues, but they may fracture the higher-dimensional structures networks actually use. This episode was made with support from Goodfire.

title: EXPOSED: India Is Training Millions in AI but Cannot Find Enough Jobs for Any of Them
summary:
India's AI Jobs Paradox: AI Skilling Boost vs Fresher Hiring Drop

While AI engineering job postings in India have surged by nearly 60% and government programs have trained over 5.4 lakh candidates in emerging technologies, net hiring across India's IT sector dropped precipitously from 6 lakh in FY22 to 1.4 lakh in FY26. A survey of 651 Indian IT enterprises revealed that 55% have reduced entry-level hiring, even as demand for senior AI architects with 6 to 10 years of experience remains intensely competitive. As AI coding agents and autonomous workflows displace routine junior tasks, India faces a structural paradox: an acute shortage of execution-ready senior talent alongside an oversupply of fresh graduates lacking production-level experience.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Anil Agarwal (Co-Founder & CEO, Incruiter) and Ramesh Pudhucode (Technology Adviser & Investment Strategist, Primerica). They unpack the decline of campus bulk hiring, the rise of AI full-stack developer roles, whether Global Capability Centres (GCCs) can replace traditional IT employment engines, and restructuring skilling incentives around verified job placements.

Is India training its workforce for a technological future that is closing its entry-level doors?

title: HUGE: Andhra Pradesh Taught 25 Lakh Adults to Read in One Year Targeting 100 Percent by 2027
summary:
Andhra Pradesh literacy rates have surged to 82.1%, with a new push to reach full coverage by 2027.

Education Minister Nara Lokesh announced significant gains under the state's Akshar Andra initiative, which successfully taught 25 lakh adults to read in just one year. This education policy coordinates 11 government departments to reach remote populations, aiming to bridge existing gaps in the regional system.

Beyond adult education, the state is tracking student progress using the LEAP app, which has already helped enrol 33,000 out-of-school children. With high teacher attendance metrics and targeted funding like the Taliki Wandam scheme, the state is aggressively pursuing its goal to improve the overall literacy rate and ensure 100 per cent school participation.

title: BREAKING: India Is Building a Protocol That Lets AI Agents Spend Your UPI Money Automatically
summary:
The NPCI is testing a Unified Agent Protocol that allows AI agents to initiate UPI payments without manual approval. Learn how this shift impacts your future financial autonomy.

The NPCI is currently developing the Unified Agent Protocol (UAP) to streamline how autonomous systems handle transactions. This system enables AI agents to perform secure transfers using existing UPI features like UPI Circle and Reserve Pay. If fully implemented, this could fundamentally change digital payments by removing the need for users to manually authorise every single grocery store checkout or bill payment.

Major players like Razorpay, Cashfree, and Pine Labs are already experimenting with similar autonomous payment structures. While this offers convenience, the transition raises critical questions regarding liability and accountability when automated systems make financial errors. Regulators are now focusing on creating a framework for AI agent verification and authorisation to prevent unauthorised spending.

title: BREAKTHROUGH: IISc Bengaluru Designs a Moon Habitat Bigger Than the ISS That Fits in One Rocket
summary:
IISc Bengaluru has designed a modular moon habitat that fits inside a single rocket, potentially reshaping the future of space exploration.

Researchers at IISc have proposed the BHEEM habitat, a modular system designed to support a crew of 16 for long-term lunar or Martian missions. By utilising a clever architecture of triangular, square, and pentagonal panels connected by specialised joints, the design maximises internal living space while simplifying assembly. This approach represents a significant shift in India’s strategy, moving from purely engineering-focused goals to solving complex human factors and logistics challenges in space.

The structure is designed to fit inside a single 800 cubic meter payload, such as a SpaceX Starship, before expanding to offer over 2,000 cubic meters of usable volume. Finite element analysis confirms the structural integrity of the design, which uses space-grade titanium alloys to withstand lunar conditions. As nations increasingly compete in the space race, this habitat concept offers a scalable solution for sustainable, long-term habitation beyond Earth.

title: BREAKING: ISRO Launches India's First Satellite That Can Watch the Entire Country Every 30 Minutes
summary:

Unlike standard imaging technology, this satellite maintains a fixed view of the region, enabling rapid repeat imaging of fast-moving events like cyclones and floods. This capability represents a significant advancement in how we track environmental changes across the country.

We break down the technical specifications, including the multispectral and hyperspectral imaging capabilities that support applications in agriculture and national security. By providing real-time data, this launch marks a major milestone in India news, building on lessons learned from previous missions to ensure reliable performance in orbit.

title: Kargo in Action
summary:
Meet the Akuity engineers who built Kargo and wrote this book, Ken Cochrane, Jesse Suen, and Kent Rancourt. 

Kargo is a Kubernetes-native application lifecycle orchestration tool that works alongside Argo CD to promote software builds, automatically moving software artifacts, container images, Helm chart versions, or Git commits from development to staging to production.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
1. Why isn't traditional CI/CD enough for modern software delivery?
2. Why should teams separate deployment from promotion?
3. How does Kargo close the gap between building software and running it safely?
4. How can teams promote the same artifact across multiple environments?
5. What is a promotion control plane, and why do teams need one?
6. How can teams add approvals without slowing every release?
7. How does Kargo make software promotions auditable?
8. How can teams trace exactly what reached each environment?
9. How does Kargo make rollbacks safer and more predictable?
10. How can teams coordinate promotions across multiple services?
11. How does Kargo work with existing GitOps tools like Argo CD?
12. How can teams customize promotion workflows without creating fragile scripts?
13. How does Kargo help organizations balance delivery speed with governance?
14. How does Kargo compare to other similar tools?
15. What is the difference between the free version of Kargo and the paid version?

title: BREAKING: India Officially Launches Semicon 2.0 to Own 10% of the Global Chip Market
summary:
Semicon 2.0 is India's new initiative to capture 10% of the global chip market. Learn the six pillars driving this national goal.

The Indian government recently detailed the strategy behind Semicon 2.0, aiming for a significant footprint in the global technology sector. This roadmap focuses on six specific pillars, including design, machines and materials, fabs, advanced packaging, research and development, and talent development. By moving beyond individual chip fabs, the plan establishes a holistic ecosystem for the India semiconductor industry.

A key metric of this progress is the rapid growth of the technical workforce. India hit its target of training 85,000 semiconductor engineers in just four years, significantly outpacing the original ten-year timeline. With a new goal set to add 100,000 more professionals, the focus remains on execution speed, with some approvals processed in 90 days and production projects starting quickly. This shift highlights a strategic commitment to scaling India chip manufacturing capabilities on a national level.

title: How to install a quantum computer
summary:
Quantum computers represent a fundamentally new paradigm in the science of computation, so it’s no surprise that quantum system installations are anything but ordinary. From cryogenic cooling to complex control electronics, deploying a quantum computer requires specialized infrastructure and expertise.  

In this episode of The Coherence Times, we sit down with John Kolb of Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and IBM’s Rajeev Malik to go behind the scenes of a unique installation: a quantum computer housed inside a restored chapel. Together, they offerrare insight into what it takes to install and operate quantum systems, how quantum fits alongside classical supercomputing, and what the future of quantum-centric supercomputing could look like as the technology scales. 

Visit IBM Quantum Platform to run circuits on real quantum hardware: https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com

title: Why Your Agent Evals Are Missing the Real Failures (with Aishwarya Srinivasan)
summary:
#AgenticAI #AIEvals #VibeCoding

In Episode #1023, Aishwarya Srinivasan (Co-Founder of The Gen Academy) joins @JonKrohnLearns to work out where a competitive moat comes from once anything you can build in ten minutes, somebody else can build in ten minutes too. Ash came to teaching through Illuminate AI, the mentorship community she started in 2020, and now trains senior engineers and leaders to ship agentic AI in production; she is blunt that vibe coding lowers the floor without touching the engineering judgment that production demands. In this episode, she explains what a whole-system eval covers that a model eval misses, traces reinforcement learning from the algorithm she patented at IBM to its resurgence in agentic fine tuning and lays out the MIND framework from her TED Talk for living with AI.

title: India Sets 8-Year Roadmap for 7nm to 3nm Chips | Tim Cook Steps Down as Apple CEO
summary:
India has established a strategic eight-year roadmap targeting advanced semiconductor nodes from 7nm down to 3nm, focusing on building indigenous chip design, domestic talent pipelines, and advanced fabrication capabilities to compete globally. In international news, Tim Cook announced he will step down as Apple CEO after 15 years, passing leadership to long-time Hardware Chief John Ternus. Meanwhile, OpenAI revoked model API access from Cursor following its $60 billion buyout by SpaceX, while also purchasing tens of thousands of Mac units to train computer-use agents. Domestically, Gnani AI unveiled the Gnani Artha sovereign AI stack, IndiGo Ventures invested ₹30 crore in Sarvam AI, Bengaluru startup Aspera launched its autonomous Eureka Seaplane, 14 Hyderabad spacetech firms pitched a shared Space City, and AIM Senior Tech Journalist Shalini Mondal joins us live.

This is your Front Page LIVE, bringing you sharp analysis of the biggest technology, business, policy and economic stories shaping India and the world.

* Tim Cook concludes a historic 15-year tenure as Apple CEO; John Ternus steps in to lead the company's AI era

* OpenAI buys tens of thousands of Mac mini and Mac Studio units to train agentic computer-use models
* Surgeons in London perform world's first live AI-guided brain surgery to successfully remove a tumor

* 14 Hyderabad spacetech startups petition the Telangana government to build a shared Space City hub
* AIM Senior Tech Journalist Shalini Mondal joins live to evaluate whether India's frugal space model can sustain future missions
